title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Maya Singh
description: Motivation: Under mixed workload conditions we observed starvation of small low-latency requests when the continuous batcher prioritized throughput-heavy long sequences. This PR introduces scheduler-level changes to improve queueing fairness, prevent starvation, and reduce tail latency by enforcing adaptive timeouts and priority aging. Summary of changes: added a deadline-aware queue, per-request priority aging, soft preemption points for long-running batches, and an adaptive per-queue timeout policy. The scheduler now tracks request enqueue time and applies an aging factor that increases effective priority over time to ensure older small requests are scheduled before they starve. We also introduced a configurable max-batch-hold timeout and a soft-preempt flag that allows long-running batches to yield at safe KV-cache boundaries. KV cache considerations: soft preemption points are implemented so that preemption only occurs after a safe KV-cache flush/checkpoint boundary to avoid cache corruption or unnecessary recomputation. The scheduler integrates with the KV cache manager via a simple lease protocol: batches acquire a short-lived cache lease and release it at preemption points. This prevents preemption from invalidating in-flight KV state. Configuration: new flags under continuous_batcher.scheduler: "max_batch_hold_ms" (default 12ms), "priority_age_ms" (default 50ms window for full aging), "enable_soft_preempt": true, and "min_batch_fill" (default 0.25). Defaults were chosen to keep baseline throughput unchanged while improving P95 latency for latency-sensitive workloads. Telemetry and observability: added metrics continuous_batcher.queue_wait_ms_bucket, continuous_batcher.preemptions_total, continuous_batcher.priority_age_distribution, and annotations in traces to mark preemption and KV lease events. Dashboard updates included in docs/architecture/continuous_batcher.md. Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on p4d instances with mixed workloads (50% short chat reqs ~32 tokens, 50% long generation ~1024 tokens) show: P50 latency unchanged, P95 latency improved ~23%, and throughput degradation <2% for default config. End-to-end canary in perf lab showed no regression on production-like traffic. Related: iterates on prior continuous-batcher fairness work (see ENG-2985) and addresses regressions surfaced in SUP-1198. Notes: This PR includes behavioral tests and an integration canary; rollout should be done as a canary followed by ramping the feature flag organization-wide.

review_discussion: Evan Carter (reviewer): Please quantify the effect on throughput for the 99th percentile across a few model sizes. Also want an explanation of how priority aging interacts with autoscaling decisions.

Maya Singh (author): Added microbench numbers in the description and new metric priority_age_distribution. Priority aging is intentionally local to scheduler decisions and does not change the request rate; autoscaling is unaffected but we added an annotation to traces so ASGs can consider queue pressure in future work.

Diego Montes (reviewer): Can we reduce contention on the KV lease path? The current implementation holds a mutex in the hot path. Requested change: switch to an atomic stamped pointer for lease state or a try-lock with backoff.
Maya Singh (author): Reworked kv_lease to use an atomic stamped state with compare-and-swap and added microbench to show negligible overhead. Pushed commit 3f9c8e0.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Tests look good; please add a canary run in perf lab and document rollout steps.
Maya Singh (author): Canary results appended to bench_continuous_batcher; rollout notes added to docs. Ready for squash-merge.
Evan Carter (approver): Approving after kv lease atomic change and perf bench results.
release_notes: Improved continuous-batcher scheduler: adaptive timeouts, priority aging to prevent starvation, soft preemption points compatible with KV cache, new telemetry. Default config preserves throughput while improving P95 latency for mixed workloads.
rollout_plan: Canary in perf lab -> staged rollout to 10% of requests with feature flag -> 50% -> 100% if canary metrics stable for 24h. Monitor continuous_batcher.preemptions_total and queue_wait_ms P99.
notes_for_oncall: If we observe increased KV-miss or cache corruption after rollout, immediately toggle feature flag enable_soft_preempt to false and roll back. Use trace annotations to locate preemption points.
